title: Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut
main_claim: For every fixed C>1 there is a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to Uniform Sparsest Cut (rational capacities, unit demand on all pairs) with YES ⇒ Φ(G) ≤ a and NO ⇒ Φ(G) > C·a. So approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any constant factor is NP-hard, with no complexity assumption.

issues.location: Sec 1 (Lemma pencil, GS tower) / Sec 5 marking rules
issues.description: Coverage caveat, not a gap. I did not re-derive the algebraic-geometry construction of the quadratic evaluation pencil (Garcia–Stichtenoth tower, lattice/determinant estimates, finite algorithm). I also did not check every union-bound constant in the three cell-marking rules and in the marking-truth estimate. A parameter count is consistent with the claim: length m=O(d), relative distance at least 1−λ0, and the squared AG code giving λ0 ≳ 2d/m + O(1/r).
issues.evidence: Lemma 1.1 (ii) needs C^{*2} for an AG code to have relative distance at least 1−λ0 while containing the standard basis. The Singleton/AG bound requires m ≥ (d+g)·2/λ0, which the tower supplies with g ≈ m/(r−1). This is consistent, but I did not check it line by line.

sibling_notes: There were no prior entries for family 117 on the board. This paper cites OpenAIUniqueGames2026 only for historical context; the main proof does not depend on it.
